title: Handle ValidationException in apiCreate with structured 422 response
description: ElementalGridController::apiCreate() calls $newElement->write() without try/catch. Either catch ValidationException and return structured JSON, or have HierarchyValidationService throw HierarchyValidationException (which the controller catches).
close_reason: Caught ValidationException in apiCreate, returning structured 422 JSON error via jsonError()

title: Add API schema extension point for element node enrichment

This includes a bridge between SilverStripe's jQuery/Entwine system and React, component registration via the Injector pattern, and blocking the stock Elemental UI JavaScript and CSS bundles.
acceptance_criteria:
React application renders inside the CMS admin where Elemental UI normally appears
Stock Elemental JS and CSS bundles are blocked and do not load
Components are registered via SilverStripe Injector pattern
Bridge handles CMS page navigation without full page reloads
close_reason: Verified implemented in codebase

title: Define frontend element type system
description: Define TypeScript types for the element hierarchy using discriminated unions. The type system must represent container types (Section, Row, Column) and simple elements as distinct variants, encode hierarchy rules (which children each container allows), and derive element status from API data.
acceptance_criteria:
Discriminated union types distinguish Section, Row, Column, and simple elements
Type system encodes which child types each container allows
Status derivation produces draft, published, and modified states from API data
TypeScript compiler catches invalid element type usage at build time
close_reason: Verified implemented in codebase

title: Implement Tailwind CSS Grid adapter
description: Implement the grid adapter for Tailwind CSS using CSS Grid layout. The adapter defines Tailwind's responsive breakpoints (sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl), generates classes like col-span-{n} for widths, col-start-{n} for offsets, and hidden/block for visibility. It returns a 12-column default and provides a path to fallback CSS for CMS preview.
acceptance_criteria:
Width classes follow col-span-{n} pattern with viewport prefix
Offset classes follow col-start-{n} pattern with viewport prefix
Visibility classes use Tailwind hidden/block utilities
Default column count is 12
close_reason: Verified implemented in codebase

title: Implement central grid config service
description: Create a service that acts as the central access point for grid configuration. It delegates to the currently bound grid adapter for framework-specific behavior but allows YAML overrides for total column count and default viewport. All other services and extensions query grid configuration through this service rather than directly accessing the adapter.
acceptance_criteria:
Service delegates to the bound adapter for class generation and viewport info
total_columns override in YAML changes the column count returned by the service
default_viewport override in YAML changes which viewport is treated as default
Other services can inject this service to query grid configuration
close_reason: Implemented GridConfigService with interface, YAML config, and full test coverage

title: Expose recursive nested element tree via API
description: Create an API endpoint that returns the complete element tree for a page, recursively including all nested children for every container. Each element in the response includes its type classification, container kind, draft/published status, edit/view permissions, and allowed child types. The response schema must be extensible. The tree builder must not invoke CMS field scaffolding per element.
acceptance_criteria:
API response contains nested children for Sections, Rows, and Columns recursively
Each element includes type classification, container kind, status, and permissions
Each container includes its list of allowed child types
Adding new fields to the response does not require changes to this endpoint
Building a tree of 50+ elements does not exhaust PHP memory limits
close_reason: Verified implemented in codebase

title: Validate cross-area moves for circular references
description: Extend the hierarchy validation to detect circular references when moving containers across ElementalAreas. A container must not be moved into its own descendant tree. The check walks the target area's ancestor chain to verify the source element does not appear in it.
acceptance_criteria:
Moving a Section into one of its own descendant Rows is rejected with a validation error
Moving a Row into a Column that belongs to that same Row is rejected
Moving a container to a valid, non-descendant area succeeds
Circular reference check works at any nesting depth
close_reason: Added 3 regression tests proving fixed hierarchy type rules prevent circular references. No new validation logic needed.

title: Implement hierarchy validation service
description: Create a validation service that enforces the 4-layer hierarchy rules using per-element-type strategy classes. Each strategy (Section, Row, Column) defines which parent types are valid, which child types are allowed, and what error to return on violation. The service is called on every element write to prevent invalid placements.
acceptance_criteria:
Saving a Section inside a Row returns a validation error
Saving a Row at page top level returns a validation error
Saving a Column directly inside a Section returns a validation error
Saving a container element inside a Column returns a validation error
Adding a new element type only requires a new strategy class (no core service changes)
close_reason: Verified implemented in codebase

title: Use proper HTTP methods in ElementalGridController url_handlers
description:
The $url_handlers in ElementalGridController currently use POST for all mutating routes. Some should use more semantically correct HTTP methods:

- POST api/create — correct (creating a resource)
- POST api/publish — should be PUT or PATCH (state change)
- POST api/unpublish — should be PUT or PATCH (state change)
- POST api/delete — should be DELETE
- POST api/duplicate — correct (creating a new resource)

Also review whether the route paths themselves follow RESTful conventions (e.g. api/elements/{id}/publish vs api/publish with id in body).
